source.notes: Paper prints: Series Z4WYX, 'SET~1' (text layer; stored as SET-1), Q.P. Code 57/4/1, 27 printed pages = 27 PDF pages (no cover offset), 33 questions, Maximum Marks 70, Time allowed 3 hours. Session is not printed on the paper. English text is on odd PDF pages (Hindi on even pages), except the cover (page 1) which mixes both. The question-paper archive lists Q.P. codes 57-1-1, 57-1-2, 57-1-3, 57-2-1, 57-2-2, 57-2-3, 57-4-1, 57-4-2, 57-4-3, 57-5-1..57-7-3 plus a Visually-Impaired paper; 57-1-1, 57-1-2, 57-1-3, 57-2-1, 57-2-2 and 57-2-3 are scanned image-only PDFs with no usable text layer (pdftotext returns ~24 characters, i.e. only page-break markers) and were skipped. 57-4-1 is the first Q.P. code in order with both a usable QP text layer and a usable matching English marking-scheme text layer (the marking scheme for 57-1-1 does have a text layer, but its question paper does not, so that pair was skipped). A handful of words are missing from the PDF text layer in isolated spots, apparently due to an embedded font/rendering issue rather than a figure (confirmed by trying default, -layout and -raw pdftotext modes, all with the same gaps): the opening clause of Q1, part of the Assertion in Q13, the subject of the Assertion in Q15, several phrases in the Q27 passage, and the compared-animal names in Q29(c). These are flagged per question and kept as extracted (marked with '[text missing in extraction]'), never invented. Prime symbols (') on 5'/3' end labels are dropped throughout the text layer (e.g. Q18's mRNA frames, Q24's 'DNA depicted in 3 end directionality'); flagged per question. Q10's four options are diagrams (DNA banding patterns after centrifugation) with no text at all; options kept as an empty array. Q24's diagram of a DNA strand is not reproduced, and its sub-part (b) text is entirely missing from the extraction (only 'Two' is recoverable from the marking scheme's answer, not inserted into the question text). Non-OR sub-parts that share one premise and have no marks printed per sub-part (Q18, Q20, Q23, Q24, Q26, Q27) are kept together as one entry, per the pack's own printed total mark for that question number; Section D's case-based Q29 and Q30 are likewise each kept as one entry with their internal 'OR' retained in the text. OR alternatives with their own printed marks (Q17, Q19, Q21, Q31, Q32, Q33) are split into separate entries sharing a choiceGroup. Q28 (advantages/disadvantages of the Green Revolution) does not correspond to any chapter in this subject's taxonomy list (which covers only genetics/physiology/microbes/biotechnology/ecology/evolution chapters, not agriculture/food-production topics); its chapter is left null.

questions.text: Explain how the immunity of a person is affected if there is atrophy (degeneration) of the thymus gland at an early stage of life.

questions.text:
The basic scheme of the essential steps involved in the process of recombinant DNA technology is summarized below in the form of a flow diagram. Study the given flow diagram and answer the questions that follow.
Step-1: Vector DNA (cut using Restriction Enzyme EcoR I) + Alien DNA (cut using Restriction Enzyme EcoR I) --[Enzyme A]-->
Step-2: Recombinant DNA molecule
Step-3: Transfer of recombinant DNA molecule in E. coli (Host)
Step-4: Replication of recombinant DNA molecule in E. coli
(a) Name the enzyme used in Step-1 to join the cut plasmid and alien DNA.
(b) State the technical term used for Step-3.
(c) Justify the use of same Restriction Enzyme EcoR I to cut both the vector DNA and the alien DNA.
extractionIssues: Flow-diagram box/arrow layout reconstructed as a linear text sequence; all step labels were present in the text layer.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) DNA ligase.
(b) Transformation.
(c) The same restriction enzyme EcoRI is used to cut both the vector DNA and alien DNA because it will produce complementary overhangs or sticky ends which will help in joining the two DNA strands through hydrogen bonds.

questions.text: Explain how the interaction between sea anemone and clownfish is one of the best examples of commensalism in nature.

officialAnswer.text: The clownfish gets protection from predators due to the presence of stinging tentacles, thus deriving benefit from the sea anemone; the sea anemone neither derives any benefit nor gets harmed from the clownfish.

questions.text: Correctly depict (also indicate the trophic level) and describe the ecological pyramid of biomass in sea with 40 standing crop of phytoplankton supporting 90 standing crop of zooplankton which further supports 120 small fishes.

officialAnswer.text: Inverted pyramid of biomass: Primary producers (PP) - 40 standing crop of phytoplankton; Primary consumers (PC) - 90 standing crop of zooplankton; Secondary consumers (SC) - 120 fishes, with increasing biomass from PP to SC. (Award 1 mark for diagram of inverted pyramid of biomass, and 1 mark for correct trophic level.)

questions.text: Explain the process of formation of placenta in a human female after the implantation of the blastocyst in the endometrium of the uterus.

officialAnswer.text: After implantation of the blastocyst, finger-like projections appear on the trophoblast, called chorionic villi, which are surrounded by the uterine tissue and maternal blood; the chorionic villi and uterine tissue become interdigitated with each other, and form a structural and functional unit between the developing embryo/foetus and maternal tissue/body called the placenta.

questions.text:
Gregor Mendel conducted hybridisation experiments in garden pea for seven years and proposed the law of inheritance.
(a) Why was he successful in his hybridisation experiments ? Give two reasons.
(b) State the law of independent assortment as proposed by Mendel after his dihybrid crosses.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) True-breeding pea plant varieties were selected; distinct contrasting characters were selected for different traits; artificial (self and cross) pollination was conducted carefully; a large sample size was used; results were confirmed by performing experiments for several generations; or any other correct point. (any two reasons)
(b) When two pairs of traits are combined in a hybrid, segregation of one pair of characters is independent of the other pair of characters.

questions.text: Explain the biological treatment of primary effluent when passed into the large aeration tanks in a sewage treatment plant (STP).

officialAnswer.text: The sewage is constantly agitated mechanically and air is pumped into it. This allows the vigorous growth of useful microbes into flocs (masses of bacteria associated with fungal hyphae, forming mesh-like structures). While growing, these microbes consume the major part of the organic matter in the effluent. This significantly reduces the Biochemical Oxygen Demand (BOD).

questions.text:
According to a recent wildlife report, the biggest threat to the tiger’s survival in Mudumalai Tiger Reserve (MTR) was found to be a small, beautiful flower, Lantana camara, a tropical American shrub, that invaded 40% of India’s tiger range. Tamil Nadu department’s Lantana weed eradication drive helped to restore the dying MTR thereby also reducing human-wildlife conflicts. MTR is home to 25 species of grasses and legumes.
Answer the given questions based on the information given above.
(a) Explain how did the removal of Lantana help in restoring the dying Mudumalai Tiger Reserve.
(b) Why is the invasion of Lantana camara a cause of concern in MTR.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) Removal of Lantana allows other plants to grow, due to which the herbivore population increases and that helps restore the tiger population.
(b) Lantana, being invasive, does not allow other plants to grow in its surroundings; this will decrease the herbivore population, which can in turn cause a decline in the tiger population.

questions.text: Enlist one advantage and two disadvantages of green revolution.

officialAnswer.text:
Advantage: Increase in the production of crops, supporting a larger population in terms of food. (any one advantage)
Disadvantages: Use of agrochemicals (fertilisers and pesticides) led to pollution of soil or water in the long run (biomagnification); crop management practices such as irrigation are expensive; agrochemicals were too expensive; led to increase in soil salinity; agrochemicals reduce natural soil fertility; crops become dependent on fertilisers and pesticides; or any other correct answer. (any two disadvantages)

questions.text:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow.
The most convincing evidence to trace evolutionary relationships between humans and different groups of animals come from the basic similarities seen at the molecular level. Study the table given below that depicts the number of amino acid differences between the haemoglobin polypeptide of few animals with that of humans and answer the questions that follow.
S.No. | Animal | No. of amino acid differences in haemoglobin with that of humans
1. | Macaque | 08
2. | Dog | 32
3. | Bird | 45
4. | Frog | 67
5. | Lamprey | 125
(a) To which category of evolution (Divergent or Convergent) do the following evolutionary relationships belong to :
(i) Humans and Macaque
(ii) Humans and Frog
(b) What do the biochemical similarities in haemoglobin suggest about the evolutionary relationship between humans, frog and lamprey ?
(c) (i) Which one of the two – lampreys’ or macaques’ evolution is more closely related to humans and why ?
OR
(c) (ii) Which one of the two – frogs’ or dogs’ evolution is more closely related to humans and why ?
extractionIssues: Table layout reconstructed from jumbled PDF text order (rows/columns realigned against the printed animal names and amino-acid-difference values); all values were present in the text layer.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) (i) Human and Macaque = Divergent evolution. (ii) Human and Frog = Divergent evolution.
(b) Biochemical similarities in haemoglobin suggest common ancestry.
(c)(i) Macaque is more closely related to humans than lamprey, because the number of amino acid differences between human and macaque is less / human and macaque have more biochemical similarities in the structure of haemoglobin than human and lamprey.
OR
(c)(ii) Dog is more closely related to human than frog, because the number of amino acid differences between human and dog is less / dog and human have more biochemical similarities in the structure of haemoglobin than human and frog.

questions.text:
Read the following passage and answer the questions that follow.
Deaths related to the use of drugs were estimated at about 5,00,000 in 2019, 17.5 percent more than in 2009. Liver diseases attributed to Hepatitis B are a major cause of drug-related deaths, according to UNODC, accounting for more than half of the total number of deaths attributed to the use of drugs. Drug overdoses account for a quarter of drug-related deaths.
Opioids contribute to account for the most severe drug-related harm, including fatal overdoses, when used non-medically. At the global level, two-third of direct drug-related deaths are due to opioids, and in some sub-regions the proportion can be as high as three-quarters of such deaths.
(a) Why are people taking opioids more prone to liver diseases attributed to Hepatitis B ?
(b) What is meant by direct drug-related disease ?
(c) (i) What is the scientific name of the plant from which the opioids are derived and from which part of the plant is it extracted ?
OR
(c) (ii) State two common warning signs of drug abuse among the youth.
extractionIssues: Decimal point dropped in extraction: printed as "17 5 percent", rebuilt as "17.5 percent"; check against the PDF.

officialAnswer.text:
(a) As opioids are generally taken intravenously, use of contaminated needles or injections increases the chances of hepatitis B (liver disease).
(b) Direct drug-related disease means diseases due to overdoses of opioids / fatal overdose of opioids.
(c)(i) Papaver somniferum; latex.
OR
(c)(ii) Drop in academic performance, unexplained absence from school or college, lack of interest in personal hygiene, withdrawal, isolation, depression, fatigue, aggressive/rebellious behaviour, deteriorating relationships with family and friends, loss of interest in hobbies, change in sleeping and eating habits, fluctuations in weight/appetite, stealing, mental and financial distress, or any other correct point. (any two signs)

questions.text:
(i) Explain how does double fertilisation take place in a flowering plant.
(ii) Write the fate of the products of double fertilization in these plants.

officialAnswer.text:
After entering one of the synergids, the pollen tube releases the two male gametes into the cytoplasm of the synergid; one male gamete moves towards the egg cell and fuses with its nucleus, completing syngamy to form the zygote; the other male gamete moves towards the two polar nuclei in the central cell and fuses with them, causing triple fusion to form the Primary Endosperm Nucleus (PEN)/Primary Endosperm Cell (PEC).
(ii) The Primary Endosperm Cell develops into the endosperm, while the zygote develops into the embryo.

questions.text:
(i) Explain the structure of testicular lobules in human male reproductive system. Name the two types of cells present in the seminiferous tubules and state their role.
(ii) Describe the role of hypothalamic hormone GnRH in spermatogenesis.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Each testicular lobule consists of 1-3 highly coiled seminiferous tubules, in which sperms are produced. Two types of cells: male germ cells/spermatogonia, which undergo meiotic divisions finally leading to sperm formation; and Sertoli cells, which provide nutrition to the germ cells.
(ii) GnRH acts at the anterior pituitary gland and stimulates secretion of two gonadotropins - luteinising hormone (LH) and follicle stimulating hormone (FSH).

questions.text: Name and explain the biotechnological strategy wherein the infection by the nematode Meloidegyne incognitia can be prevented using Agrobacterium vectors in the roots of tobacco plant by RNA interference.

officialAnswer.text: RNA interference (RNAi). Steps: Using Agrobacterium vectors, nematode-specific genes were introduced into the host plants. The introduction of DNA was such that it produced both sense and anti-sense RNA in the host cells. The two complementary RNAs form a double-stranded RNA (dsRNA), which initiated RNAi and silenced the specific mRNA of the nematode (consequently the parasite could not survive in a transgenic host expressing the specific interfering RNA).

questions.text: Explain the amplification of gene of interest using the technique of Polymerase chain reaction (PCR).

officialAnswer.text: Each cycle in PCR has three steps - denaturation, annealing, extension. Denaturation: DNA is subjected to high temperature, and the two strands of DNA separate due to broken hydrogen bonds between nitrogenous bases. Annealing: two sets of primers, which are complementary, attach on the 3' end of both template strands. Extension: a new strand of DNA is formed using the thermostable Taq polymerase enzyme (derived from Thermus aquaticus), which extends the primers using the nucleotides provided in the reaction and the genomic DNA as template. The process is repeated about 30 times; the segment of DNA is amplified about 1 billion times, i.e. 1 billion copies are made. (Marks to be allotted if the key points are depicted in the form of a diagram.)

questions.text:
(i) Describe the population growth curve applicable in a population of any species in nature that has limited resources at its disposal.
(ii) Give the equation of this growth curve.
(iii) Name the growth curve and depict a graphical plot for this type of population growth.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) A population growing in a habitat with limited resources initially shows a lag phase, followed by phases of acceleration and deceleration, and finally an asymptote when the population density reaches the carrying capacity.
(ii) [equation image not reproduced in the marking scheme's text layer] (N = population density at time t, r = intrinsic rate of natural increase, k = carrying capacity)
(iii) Logistic growth curve / Verhulst-Pearl Logistic Growth curve / sigmoid growth curve / S-shaped curve. [graphical plot image not reproduced]

questions.text:
(i) Explain the Species-Area relationship within a natural forest and also predict the nature of graph when species richness is plotted against the area for a wide variety of taxa.
(ii) Depict the graphical relationship between species richness and area.
(iii) Give the equation of the Species-Area relationship for a wide variety of taxa on a logarithmic scale.

officialAnswer.text:
(i) Within a region, species richness increases with increasing explored area, but only up to a limit. Nature of the graph: rectangular hyperbola.
(ii) [graph image not reproduced in the marking scheme's text layer]
(iii) log S = log C + Z log A (S = Species richness, A = Area, Z = slope of the line/regression coefficient, C = Y-intercept)
